newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA cuts Finnish 1997 CPI forecast to 1 pct.
newsitem.headline: ETLA cuts Finnish 1997 CPI forecast to 1 pct.

text.p: The Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) on Wednesday lowered its 1997 CPI inflation forecast to one percent from two percent and reduced its 1997 unemployment forecast to 15.5 percent from 16 percent.
ETLA left its Finnish 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast unchanged at 3.5 percent and its 1996 GDP growth forecast unrevised at 2.5 percent.
"Inflation will remain low and it appears that there is no reason to tighten monetary policy until towards the end of next year," ETLA said in a statement.
"The unemployment rate will decline slightly faster than previously forecast due, among other things, to increased job training programs," it said.
ETLA lowered its forecast for 1996 CPI to 0.5 percent from one percent, but kept its 1996 unemployment forecast unchanged at 16.5 percent.
It said the slump in industry had already bottomed out, and industrial output had started to rise during the autumn.

ETLA said that Finland was on track to fulfill the criteria for European economic and monetary union EMU and revised its 1997 forecast for total public debt relative to GDP down to 59.5 percent from the 63.3 percent it forecast in September.
It predicted the government's 1997 deficit to GDP, as required for membership in the EMU, would be down to 2.2 percent, revising its earlier deficit forecast of 2.5 percent.

"The balancing of public finances is proceeding well and Finland appears to fulfill all of the EMU criteria," ETLA said and it also revised downwards its EMU-relevant public debt and deficit predictions for 1996.

In its other main forecasts, ETLA said it expected export growth to strengthen in the last quarter, bringing goods export growth for full year 1996 to two percent, which is lower than the three percent it predicted in September.
"If international growth picks up as expected, this will create fertile conditions for export growth in 1997," ETLA said and repeated its earlier forecast for five percent export growth next year.
ETLA said next year's export growth would be fueled by growth in the paper industry and the metal and engineering sector.
It also said it expected firmer prices for forest industry products: "The decline in pulp and fine paper prices is already over, which indicates that demand will recover in the next few months."
ETLA said it expected goods imports to increase next year faster than this year, by about six percent, after predicted growth of four percent this year.
ETLA said that the terms of trade might strengthen towards the end of next year after declining by one percent in 1996.
